newsitem.title: USA: HUBCO withdraws merger offer to Broad Natl.
newsitem.headline: HUBCO withdraws merger offer to Broad Natl.

text.p: HUBCO Inc said Monday it had withdrawn its March 5 offer to enter into merger talks with Broad National Bancorp.
HUBCO Executive Vice President Lynn Van Borkulo-Nuzzo said the company withdrew its offer because Broad National had made the matter public.
"We believe that such matters should remain confidential," she said.
HUBCO had wanted the matter to remain secret until the companies had reached an agreement to merge, she said.
Van Borkulo-Nuzzo said HUBCO had "no particular plans right now" to try to enter into talks again with Broad National, a commercial bank.
Broad National officials were not available for comment.
The Nasdaq National Market halted trading in Broad National, pending news, at 0911 EST. The last sale was at 14.
HUBCO stock was down 3/8 at 25-7/8 in early trading.
HUBCO is a holding company for Hudson United Bank and Lafayette American Bank and Trust Co.

Later, in a statement from Newark, Broad National said on March 7 it received an unsolicited proposal from HUBCO to enter into discussions for the acquisition of Broad National in an exchange of 0.76 share of stock of HUBCO for each share of Broad.

In response to the offer, Donald Karp, chairman and chief executive of Broad National Bancorporation, said he advised HUBCO that if Broad National's board should make a decision to enter into merger negotiations with HUBCO, Broad would likely consider alternative proposals.
But he said the board had not made any decision that a sale of Broad National was preferable to remaining independent at this time.
Following that response, Broad said it received notice from HUBCO today that HUBCO's proposal was withdrawn.
Broad National is based in Newark and is the parent company of the $533 million-asset Broad National Bank.
